articles.title_orig: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
articles.title_zh: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
articles.content_orig:
For the first time, new-energy vehicles (NEVs) made up 67% of new car sales in China in September, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).
The figures show that NEVs, which include battery electric cars and plug-in hybrids, captured a record share of sales, even though fewer were sold than last year.
This is because sales of combustion-engine cars are falling steeply, a trend that the CPCA has attributed to rising petrol prices following the start of the Hormuz crisis .
Indeed, sales of fuel-only cars were down 31% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, with plug-in hybrid sales down 26% – whereas battery EV sales were only down 4%.
One analyst tells Carbon Brief that China’s rapidly growing EV fleet has offset demand for 143m barrels of oil since the start of the Hormuz crisis.
Another says that the crisis is “reinforcing China’s electrification of road transport”.
Meanwhile, amid slowing domestic sales, Chinese carmakers’ exports of NEVs more than doubled [in 2026 to date / in September] from a year earlier.
A record two out of every three cars sold in September in China were NEVs, according to CPCA data, as shown in the figure below.
(NEVs predominantly include battery electric vehicles – BEVs – and plug-in hybrids  – PHEVs. BEVs only run on electricity, whereas PHEVs also have a combustion engine.)
This marks a rapid rise for NEVs from just 6% of new car sales in 2020 up to 58% in 2026 to date – and a record 67% in the month of September.
This year, NEVs’ share of sales has also bounced back from a low of 39% in January, after the full purchase tax exemption that had been in place for more than a decade came to an end in December 2025.
The gain in NEV share in 2026 has come amid a slowdown across the wider domestic passenger-car market, which has hit sales of combustion-engine vehicles particularly hard.
This September, passenger-car retail sales across all categories declined, with overall sales volumes falling 28% year-on-year.
The contraction was led by combustion-engine vehicles, which saw sales fall 43% year-on-year in September and 31% in 2026 to date.
However, sales of PHEVs also fell by 36% year-on-year in September and by 26% in 2026 to date. By comparison, BEVs performed better, although sales still declined 8.5% from a year earlier in September and 4% in 2026 to date.
As a result, NEV sales overall fell by 17% in September and 13% in 2026 to date.
While the market changes in 2026 to date were particularly dramatic, they reflect a broad continuation of trends seen over the past decade.
Indeed, sales of combustion-engine cars in China peaked in 2017 and they have been declining ever since, shown in the figure below.
Part of the reason for the advance of NEVs in 2026, said Chinese technology news outlet OFweek , was petrol cars “giving up market share” as they were outperformed by electric alternatives.
Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the CPCA, cited higher petrol prices as an explanation for September’s weak combustion-car sales, in comments to financial news outlet National Business Daily .
Imports of oil into China in January-September have fallen 15% compared to 2025, equivalent to 470m barrels, as ongoing conflict tightened supply and drove up prices.
China’s passenger-car NEV fleet has displaced 143m barrels of oil so far during the strait of Hormuz crisis, Euan Graham , senior energy analyst at thinktank Ember , tells Carbon Brief.
EVs “accounted for 12% of the decrease in China’s oil use post-Hormuz”, according to an estimate provided to thinktank the Brookings Institute by an unnamed analyst.
Erica Downs , a senior research scholar at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy , tells Carbon Brief that the strait of Hormuz crisis and higher oil prices are “reinforcing China’s electrification of road transport”.
She says the “world’s largest oil supply disruption” vindicates China’s early bet on EVs, which was partly driven by concerns about oil-supply security.
Nevertheless, NEV sales have fallen year-on-year, albeit at a slower rate than overall car sales. The growth in NEV market share has also been decelerating.
Zhang Yichao , a partner at consulting firm AlixPartners , tells Carbon Brief that NEVs benefit from government trade-in policies and a “strong pipeline” of new models, particularly those involving innovation.
He says these factors help explain why NEVs sales have fallen at a slower rate to their combustion-car counterparts.
Cui told the state-run China National Radio that the fall for NEVs and for cars overall in September 2026, is also due to a high baseline of sales from the same month in 2025, as well as changes to trade-in policies and disruptions from the holiday period.
Other factors, says consulting firm Wood Mackenzie , are the weakened demand due to “demand pull-forward” in 2025 caused by the end of subsidies, as well as “tighter financing conditions”.
Zhang tells Carbon Brief he does not “see much more room ahead” for further growth in NEVs’ market share.
He adds that, in his view, their share in China is unlikely to exceed 80%, as some premium-market segments and specific use cases will continue to require combustion-engine vehicles.
Meanwhile, while domestic NEV retail sales fell 17% in September 2026, exports more than doubled, increasing 164% year-on-year, according to the CPCA .
This extends the decline in domestic sales and very strong growth in exports seen across 2026 to date, as shown in the figure below.
In September, 1,084,000 NEVs were sold domestically in China, while 558,000 NEVs were exported.
Exports are becoming increasingly important to Chinese carmakers, in the face of weaker domestic demand and cut-throat industrial competition.
The CPCA says exports have become “a core priority” for some carmakers.
However, the surge in exports from China has created concern in the EU, which has placed tariffs on imports of EVs from China and recently agreed plans to cut imports of hybrids.
Countries including Mexico and Turkey have also placed tariffs on Chinese EV imports.
At the same time, the Chinese government is putting policies in place that might be expected to disincentivise exports, such as cutting VAT export rebates.
Analysts differ on what impact this policy shift will have, with some saying it will be limited, while others believe it could cause the price of exported cars to rise.

articles.title_orig: Russia, Ukraine agree to Oleshky ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump, White House says
articles.title_zh: Russia, Ukraine agree to Oleshky ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump, White House says
articles.content_orig:
People in Russian-occupied city facing severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with some reportedly surviving on weeds
The White House has said that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, where a deepening humanitarian crisis has left thousands of civilians struggling to survive.
In a statement on Friday, the White House said both sides had agreed to halt all military operations in the city from 29 October to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and preparations for the evacuation of civilians.
Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, which has been under Russian occupation since February 2022, have described increasingly desperate conditions amid severe shortages of food, water and electricity. An estimated 2,000 people remain in the city, with some reportedly forced to survive on weeds, boiled grass, bread and meagre rations.
Both Russian and Ukrainian officials said all sides were close to agreeing to a ceasefire.
The White House statement said the ceasefire was brokered by Melania Trump , and her representative worked directly with ​Russian and Ukrainian ‌leadership to define the ​terms. “Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” the first lady said.
Despite the claim the ceasefire had been brokered by Melania Trump, there had already been protracted efforts to organise a humanitarian ceasefire, with claims by Ukrainian officials that it had been Russia that had rejected previous calls.
Calls for a ceasefire had been issued by Pope Leo XIV – who discussed the issue with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy – the United Nations, EU officials and the Council of Europe . As recently as 18 October, Ukraine’s ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, had also said he thought agreement was close without any mention of the first lady’s involvement.
Ukraine has for weeks been pushing for a civilian evacuation from Oleshky and nearby settlements, at times using drones to airdrop emergency food and medical supplies into town.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces continue to report widespread disruptions to the Starlink satellite network , despite Donald Trump’s claim that Elon Musk had lifted restrictions on the service.
The slowdown, which has affected the communications system used by Ukrainian troops, began last week after Trump and Elon Musk, the founder of Starlink, publicly criticised Zelenskyy over continued strikes on Russian oil refineries.
The restrictions have raised questions and confusion about who ordered the slowdown and why, with Trump and Musk denying responsibility. Asked about the Starlink slowdowns on Friday, Trump said he would speak to Musk if the restrictions remained in place.
“I’ve heard it was fixed, but if it’s not, I’ll speak to him,” he told reporters.
Ukrainian officials said throughout the day on Friday that speeds remained capped at about 100mph, with no indication that the restrictions had been lifted.
“At present, we have not observed any lifting of the restrictions on Starlink,” said Serhii Beskrestnov, a military expert who advises Zelenskyy.
“There have been isolated cases in which Starlink has operated at speeds slightly above the imposed limits, but this is likely due to SpaceX’s algorithms or specific conditions of use, rather than any lifting of the restrictions,” Beskrestnov added.
The speed restrictions have prevented Ukrainian military equipment, including drones, from maintaining a connection to the satellite network when travelling at high speeds, hampering offensive drone operations and efforts to intercept incoming Russian attacks.

The slowing down of Starlink, coupled with Zelenskyy’s complaints that Washington had temporarily suspended intelligence-sharing with Kyiv, has plunged relations between Ukraine and the US to a new low in recent days.
Tensions first flared after Washington’s surprise decision to lift sanctions on Russia and begin importing Russian diesel , as Trump sought to bring down US energy prices before the midterm elections. Maritime tracking data showed that the first tanker carrying Russian diesel was en route to New York on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Russia launched another overnight barrage against Ukraine, even as Moscow said a fresh round of US-brokered talks aimed at ending the war could take place next month.
The Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said on Friday that trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US were expected to resume in Abu Dhabi in November. Previous rounds of negotiations have failed to produce a breakthrough, with Moscow and Kyiv far away over the terms of any peace settlement.
Among Russia’s maximalist demands are that Ukraine withdraw its forces from territory it still controls in the east of the country, drastically reduce the size of its military and adopt a neutral status that would rule out Nato membership.
Speaking to a Russian state television reporter late on Thursday, Putin once again questioned Ukraine’s sovereignty, echoing claims he has repeatedly made throughout the war. “The lands lost by Kyiv are not their territory, they are Russia’s historical lands,” Putin said.
The Russian president also cited unspecified genetic research to revive his longstanding claim that Russians and Ukrainians were “one people”, before insisting that Moscow would achieve all the objectives of its full-scale invasion.

articles.title_orig: American Express to Cut 5% of Global Workforce
articles.title_zh: American Express to Cut 5% of Global Workforce
articles.content_orig:
American Express is cutting thousands of employees as the leading credit card company prepares for artificial intelligence to take over more of its internal processes.
Amex is eliminating 5% of its global workforce and taking a $336 million restructuring charge, CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts Friday on the company's third-quarter earnings call. The firm had almost 77,000 employees at the end of 2025.
Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec told CNBC in an interview that the restructuring was to make American Express "leaner, more agile, and also to prepare for AI."
"You don't want to automate processes that are not optimally structured," Le Caillec said. "So what we're doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years."
The Amex announcement reflects a broader trend across financial services, where banks are working to replace repetitive roles with AI automation. On Thursday, Barclays confirmed plans to trim 5,000 jobs — also roughly 5% of its staff — in another tech-driven cost initiative. The moves come even as the sector is enjoying robust profits from growing consumer spending and resilient credit.
During the analyst call, Squeri said that the charge was to improve the company's efficiency.
"We've got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over the next few years, we needed to become [a] more agile and efficient organization," Squeri said.
Squeri devoted a 10-minute section of his prepared remarks to his views on AI, focusing mainly on how it will be used to personalize experiences and offers for Amex cardholders.
While the CEO emphasized the need to meet customers' desires to use AI, including agents, he added that Amex is "not going to let assistants run rogue through our system."
"We need to protect our customers [and] merchants, and we're only going to allow agents to access our systems that are either approved through API or MCP channels," he said, citing two ways to securely connect outside platforms with Amex systems.
Amex posted quarterly results that topped Wall Street profit expectations. Adjusted earnings per share were $4.68, topping the $4.48 average estimate of analysts, according to LSEG.
The company raised its full-year earnings guidance to a range of $18.30 to $18.60 per share, on an unadjusted basis, up from its previous target of $17.30 to $17.90.
That metric was helped by proceeds from Amex's sale of its stake in Global Business Travel Group , part of which went into the restructuring plan, Le Caillec said.
Total revenue rose 9% to $20.06 billion, also coming in slightly below Wall Street's $20.12 billion LSEG forecast. Executives attributed part of the spending drag to recent exits from small business co-brand partnerships.
Shares of the card company fell roughly 3% in morning trading.

articles.title_orig: Six shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
articles.title_zh: Six shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
articles.content_orig:
Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, after gunmen opened fire on a church, officials have said.
At least 34 others were injured in the church in the village of Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday.
The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing, in what government spokesperson Dr al-Momani Mohammad described as a "heinous attack".
Jordan's King Abdullah II said the authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties."
Dozens of people had been inside the church for the funeral when the shooting began, Khaled Burqan, one of the mourners, told Jordan's al-Mamlaka state-run TV.
He said two attackers armed with a rifle and a pistol had been firing at the mourners for several minutes.
In a news conference, Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya described the incident as a "terrorist" act carried out by a "group of extremists" and said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators.
He added that the incident was "painful and horrific" and "unparalleled in the history of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan".
No-one has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.
Initial reports from Jordanian officials indicated seven people had been killed in the attack. A government spokesperson later said six people had died, before officials again revised the death toll to seven.
CCTV footage, verified by the BBC, appears to shows three gunmen making their way from a road toward the church.
Two of the attackers are seen making their way onto what appears to be a vehicle entrance to the church grounds, before retreating briefly and returning with a third man. All three appear to be armed with handguns.
Separate footage believed to be from the aftermath of the attack appears to show several dead and wounded bodies on the ground amid some chaotic scenes.
There was a heavy security presence at the entrance to a hospital treating people injured in the incident in Karak, amid an atmosphere charged with anger among residents of the governorate, particularly the families of those injured and killed.
In his post on X, King Abdullah II offered his condolences to the families of the victims, writing: "Whoever imagines that the bullets of treachery can divide the ranks of Jordanians will fail in his endeavour before our steadfastness and unity."
Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun, a Christian head of state, said the "heinous terrorist attack" on the church "violated the sanctity of death and funeral mourners, contradicts all religious and humanitarian values," according to Lebanese media.
Karak has a sizeable Christian community in the majority-Muslim Jordan.
Such violence is rare in Jordan, but deadly attacks have been carried out in the country in the past.
Additional reporting by Husam Assal, BBC Arabic.

articles.title_orig: Dow tumbles 500 points as Middle East tensions rise, selling broadens beyond tech: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Dow tumbles 500 points as Middle East tensions rise, selling broadens beyond tech: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
The Dow slid on Friday as a sell-off in tech in the prior session shifted to other areas of the market and U.S. oil prices topped $100 a barrel amid rising fears that the U.S.-Iran conflict would flare up again.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 513 points, or 1%, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.1%. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.3%.
More defensive stocks came under pressure on Friday, with the consumer staples, utilities and healthcare sectors all lower. Dow component American Express fell more than 3% after announcing it was cutting about 5% of its global workforce , citing the need to "prepare for AI." Caterpillar also edged down about 2%, while Goldman Sachs fell around 1%, adding pressure to the 30-stock index.
On Thursday, many technology stocks had pulled back as traders assessed the impact of outsized corporate borrowing and rising rates on AI and other tech names. Microsoft ticked higher on Friday. However, chip stocks such as Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices were making a stronger move, with gains of 4% and 2%, respectively.
"For the last two weeks, investors have been sprinting from tech stocks and data center beneficiary stocks to safe stuff, and eventually, you run out of people willing to do that sprint, and that's what today looks like and feels like," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNBC.
Ellerbroek added that tech companies' earnings have proven strong this season, giving investors a reason to embrace tech stocks and focus less on emotion-based flights to safety.
"Emotion and fear play a really big role," the investor said. But, "we've gotten a few tech companies' [latest quarterly financial reports] and their earnings results have been good."
The 10-year Treasury yield was steady at around 4.994%. The benchmark yield had fallen below the key 5% level on Thursday for the first time in a month as investors grew cautious about the massive borrowing that is underway to finance the building of AI data centers.
Oil prices also rose on Friday, further pressuring stocks. West Texas Intermediate futures were up more than 3% to $102.98 per barrel. Brent crude prices rose 3.5% to $117.10. It follows reports that the U.S. and Israel may be drawing up plans for renewed attacks on Iran as part of the regional war that started in late February. Iran has countered that it is prepared to strike back as well.
On the week, the S&P 500 is heading for a slim loss, down less than 0.1%, while the Nasdaq is down 0.2% in the period. The Dow is tracking for a narrow 0.7% advance.
Stocks outside the AI trade are taking the lead.
The S&P 500 Excluding AI index closed Thursday up 12.4% this year, edging out the S&P 500's roughly 12% gain. The gap has converged largely in October.
The ex-AI index is up about 6.6% in October, while the S&P 500, weighed down by concerns around AI financing, is down roughly 0.4%.
The move suggests some leadership broadening beyond AI-linked mega cap names that have dominated in recent periods. By sector, Energy and Consumer Staples are each up double digits in October while Information Technology and Communication Services lead lower, each down more than 5%.
Morgan Stanley reduced its price target on CoreWeave to $70 from $99 Friday, citing mounting financial pressures the so-called neocloud company is facing. The new target still implies 26% upside from Thursday's close.
Shares of CoreWeave, down 2% on Friday, have sold off over the past week amid investor fears over its massive artificial intelligence-rated debt. Its bond yields have also jumped, while the spread on its credit default swaps — which are insurance against default — has widened to levels generally considered distressed.
Morgan Stanley believes CoreWeave's execution has been solid and said it "remains the speed and scale leader in a crowded neocloud ecosystem."
"However, growing financing uncertainty reduces visibility into the path to deploying existing contracted capacity and achieving 8 GW [gigawatts] (active) longer-term," said analyst Adam Wood, who maintained his equal-weight rating on the stock.
He sees a multitude of outcomes for CoreWeave's future financing, "though the most reasonable path forward would likely be through securing a portion of the financing via a hyperscaler agreement to obtain a more attractive rate."
Consumer sentiment changed little in October from historically low levels as inflation weighed on the economic outlook, according to a University of Michigan survey released Friday.
The survey showed the headline consumer sentiment index at 48 for the end of the month, off just 0.1 point from September and better than the Dow Jones consensus for 46.3. Compared with a year ago, the gauge tumbled 10.4%.
Current conditions sentiment declined 8.3% monthly but the expectations measure rose 5.4% and was off just 3% from the same period in 2025.
On inflation, the one-year outlook rose to 4.7%, while the five-year expectation accelerated to 3.5%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than September.
Wall Street firm Seaport reiterated its bearish call on Nvidia with a sell rating and its price target on the stock of $180 per share, below Nvidia's Thursday closing price of $212.
While analyst Jay Goldberg thinks the AI leader is heading into 2027 "in a good position," he's concerned about the bottleneck of the power and the overall construction of data center buildout given the lack of electricians, gas turbines and gigawatt capacity, he wrote in a Thursday research note.
The firm is also worried about the risk of Nvidia over taxing its balance sheet as the company added $250 billion in commitments last quarter to secure supply chain capacity and facilitate data center construction.
At the same time, Seaport acknowledges their take "could be wrong" as Nvidia can leverage is "supply chain heft." Shares of Nvidia were flat in pre-market trading on Friday.
The three major indexes opened lower on Friday.
The S&P 500 shed 0.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 1%, or 535 points. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.5%.
The Cboe Market Volatility Index climbed another 6% Friday, rising to 20.24, after jumping 14% Thursday to 19.03.
For the week, the VIX — widely called Wall Street's "fear gauge" — is on track to close above 20 for the first time since early June. Last week, the VIX, which measures the market's expectation of 30-day forward implied volatility based on S&P 500 index options, soared 34.7% to close at 19.99, the largest one-week gain also since early June.
Here are the stocks making the biggest moves before the bell.
Moderna – Shares are down 5.7% Friday morning after falling 25% on Thursday following a leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck . Both stocks faltered even though the full data which was released Thursday appeared meaningful for patients and positive relative to Wall Street expectations.
Deckers – Shares of the shoemaker are down 6.7% after it reported fiscal second quarter earnings late Thursday that missed analyst expectations. Revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30 was $1.43 billion compared to the $1.51 Wall Street was expecting. Revenue from top brands including HOKA and UGG missing FactSet expectations.
SpaceX — Shares of the Elon Musk space and AI company were also getting a boost from an upgrade on Wall Street. PhillipCapital double upgraded the shares to buy from sell, raising its price target all the way to $250 from $75, citing surprising gains for its AI business. The new price target represents a 70% gain from here.
Bloom Energy – Shares are down 2.5% after the energy technology solutions provider for data centers reported third quarter earnings late Thursday. Despite beating on the top and bottom line and raising its full-year 2026 earnings per share guidance, what stirred fear among investors was the reported negative free cash flow for the quarter.

articles.title_orig: Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
articles.title_zh: Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
articles.content_orig:
Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
Arcane Journal – The River of Bones is packed with new background and rules. Having learnt about the lore earlier in the week, we sat down with the Warhammer: The Old World studio to discover more about the rules.
JTY: There’s a wealth of new content in this Arcane Journal, both for Tomb Kings of Khemri and Wood Elf Realms players, as well as magic items and battlefield rules for everyone. But you won’t need this supplement in order to use the new Tomb Kings models – the profiles for all of those can be found in Ravening Hordes .*
Dave: Arcane Journal – The River of Bones contains two new scenarios. The first is a multi-player Battle March scenario for four players, and the second recreates the battle on the banks of the Crystal Mere, the mysterious lake in the heart of Athel Loren where the Tomb Kings and Wood Elves clashed. Alongside these is a really fun table of rules for Enchanted Terrain , the type of thing a traveller might encounter in the depths of Athel Loren. This can be good or bad depending on what you roll. A low roll might see a unit covered in Clawing Mud suffer modifiers to its Movement, or fall subject to Stupidity due to a Fungal Enchantment . But a high roll can result in a unit gaining Regeneration after discovering the Waters of Rejuvenation , or getting a Ward save after securing the Blessings of the Ancient Wood .
JTY: In the Champions of Nehekhara section you’ll find new rules for using the Tomb Kings of Khemri in games of Battle March. For example, the Arch Hierophant enables players to field a Battle March army without having to have a Hierophant on the battlefield. Instead, the army is empowered by the machinations of a more distant Liche Priest. This gives more freedom when writing your muster list because you aren’t obliged to include two characters, whilst still allowing you to resurrect slain models as normal. Although, of course, this is not without risk…
Dave: Speaking of muster lists, Arcane Journal – The River of Bones contains two new Armies of Infamy. The first focuses on the Tomb Kings themselves, in particular the Barrow Kingdoms. These are the long forgotten vassal states of ancient Nehekhara, the fringes of a vast empire conquered in Settra’s lifetime, where occupying armies merged with those of barbarian warlords keen to emulate the practices of Nehekhara in everything from religion and burial rites to organising an army.
Where this army differs from the norm is in the options. Liche Priests gain access to the Lores of Battle Magic and Dark Magic , the better to represent the sorts of shaman common in these ancient realms, whilst both Skeleton Horsemen and Skeleton Chariots** can be upgraded, making them the ideal hard-hitting bodyguard to accompany a long dead scion of the Great Land.
JTY: But that’s not all, there’s also an Army of Infamy for the Wood Elf Realms, the Spirits of the Forest. This army focuses on the more magical elements of Athel Loren, encouraging armies that contain lots of Dryads, Treekin and Treemen. In terms of special rules, the list gives players access to Blessings of the Elder Wood , a number of magical upgrades for their Treemen and Branchwraiths , effectively giving them access to their own unique magic items.
This is followed by rules for Wood Elf Kindreds, the various clans associated with different parts of the great forest. These reflect how Kinbands, or units, from different Kindreds fight. The Kinbands of Cavaroc , for example, gain Vanguard, whilst the Kinbands of Torgovann get to choose a non-magical combat weapon and improve its AP.
The Kinbands of Cavaroc (+15 points per unit)
Kinbands that hail from the open plains of Cavaroc are swift of foot, capable of covering vast distances in a single march.
A unit belonging to this Kindred gains the Vanguard special rule and improves the Movement characteristic of the unit and their mounts (should they have one) by 1.
The Kinbands Of Torgovann (+1 points per model)
Sharing their realm with the Forge of Starlight, the Kindreds of Torgovann are armed with the finest weapons to be found in Athel Loren.
Choose one non-magical combat weapon wielded by this unit and improve the Armour Piercing characteristic of that weapon by 1. The chosen weapon must be clearly noted on your muster list.
Dave: Finally, there is a brand new set of common magic items, this time themed around the sort of ancient artefact that might be found in the depths of a long-forgotten barrow mound somewhere in the foothills of the Vaults of the Grey Mountains.
As usual, this section includes magic weapons, armour, talismans and banners, as well as enchanted and arcane items, all of which are very useful, but many of which bear an unfortunate curse!*** Take the Armour of Dust , for example; this suit of full plate armour reduces the wearer’s Toughness if they roll a 1 when making an armour save. Or there’s the vial of Barrow Dirt , a single-use item which the bearer can throw at the enemy like a Breath Weapon, with Strength 3, an AP of -3 and Multiple Wounds (2). articles.title_orig: 61 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Halloween Sale' (Europe)
articles.title_zh: 61 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Halloween Sale' (Europe)
articles.content_orig:
After Nintendo of America launched its ' Screaming Deals ' sale earlier this week, we knew it wouldn't be long before Europe followed suit.
The 'Halloween Sale' is now live for those in Europe, with delicious discounts on a boatload of titles available until 1st November . So, naturally, we have assembled the following list to make things a little more manageable.
Below, you will find every game in the Halloween Sale that we rated a 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick from all the games that fall below this review bar. We've listed things alphabetically and given the discounted price, so you know what you're paying for each.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 854k
As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store .
Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
Alien: Isolation is a survival horror masterpiece and straight-up one of the very best horror video games ever released.
It's a nerve-wracking affair — a slow, methodical game of cat and mouse against a brilliantly clever recreation of one of cinema's most infamous killers — but if you're up to the task you'll find one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences in the genre; a brilliant and beautiful homage to one of the greatest sci-fi movies of all time.
Feral Interactive has done a stellar job with this Switch port and the excellent motion controls and inclusion of all previously-released DLC only go to sweeten the deal. This is essential stuff for survival horror fans.
Developer Shared Memory's stated goal was “to craft complete experiences that will be playable long after the world loses its internet connection,” and screen after screen, Animal Well excels in delighting your eyes and giving your brain something to stew on.
It’s a riposte against a culture of post-launch updates in favour of a meticulously crafted, singular vision with potentially years’ worth of discoveries baked in. By all indications, Animal Well delivers on that long-term promise and does so with a one-of-a-kind elegance.
BlazBlue CentralFiction Special Edition may have arrived a few years late on Switch, but that delay didn't dull the sharpness of its 2D fighting package.
Not only does it give the Ragna saga a proper send-off with a story mode that's so rich in character development it could be a full anime season in its own right, but it offers a staggering number of modes to keep you playing long after the credits roll. It runs silky-smooth docked or in handheld modes and runs like a dream online.
The lack of an English dub still rankles, and new adopters are going to have to do a lot of research to understand what's going on, but it's well worth the effort.
BlazBlue: Cross Tag Battle is an utterly accomplished 2D fighting game. It's bursting with content and featuring the visual spectacle of combat that uses up every single trick in the book. A few strange decisions aside, this title is a must for fighting game fans.
Even if you're not a fan of any of the franchises represented in this game, you most certainly will be by the time you're done with this stacked fighting package.
If Blue Prince were only about finding Room 46 and nabbing your inheritance, it would be a neat little puzzler with some fun twists along the way. For those who dive in headfirst and keep track of everything else it throws at you, however, it is so much more than that.
Rarely has a game made us feel more clever, more lost, and more elated the deeper into it we ventured, and still some question marks remain over its deeper mysteries. Minor technical drops and a lack of cross-save aside, this remains a superb achievement and one of the finest head scratchers we've had the pleasure of playing.
It looks like The Witness and it plays a bit like StreetPass Garden , but Botany Manor blooms into something that's not only entirely its own, but also something quite special. Don't let its cosy aesthetics fool you — Botany Manor is packed with nicely challenging, well-designed puzzles, and isn't afraid to tackle heavy subjects, too.
Chained Echoes is a wonderful mash-up of '90s JRPG tropes, masterfully woven together to produce an experience that feels simultaneously nostalgic and fresh. A well-paced story, unconventional progression system, tactical combat system, and expansive world all come together to make for a game that is shockingly one of the very best RPGs that we played in 2022.
Really, there’s no place where it feels like Chained Echoes drops the ball, which is all the more impressive when you consider that the vast majority of it was put together by one person. It stands as a shining example of everything that makes RPGs great.
As an adventure game, Chicory: A Colorful Tale is quite sincerely up there with the very best of the genre.
There’s plenty to see and do and a full completion run will probably take you 25-30 hours. The characters and their travails are rich and likeable, the game’s sense of humour is generally inspired, and it’s all very sweet without being sugary-twee and talking down to the player. It’s also an affecting little tearjerker that will definitely strike a chord if you make art, and almost certainly will even if you don’t – so long as you’re capable of pretty basic empathy.
Chicory is simple to play but impressively long and complex, with perfect controls, performance and visuals. Throw yourself into painting the world and you’ll be left with a game that’s very much your own and speaks to you directly – a beautiful marriage of mechanics, themes and visuals.
While it’s a shame that there are fewer games here than in other Konami collections — we’d have loved to have seen NES title Contra Force or the now-extinct WiiWare title Contra ReBirth — the ones included in the Contra Anniversary Collection are universally brilliant. The 8-bit and 16-bit Contra games are among the finest examples of the run ‘n gun genre, and to have almost all of them included in a single release and emulated flawlessly is an absolute treat.
Whether you’re a fan of the series or a curious onlooker who’s always wanted to see what the fuss was all about, this is essential.
We really like Crawl , and we’d bet our collected stash of gold and wrath you will, too. A dungeon-crawling hack-and-slash affair with roguelike elements, one player is the hero trying to get through a dungeon and the others play as monster-controlling ghosts attempting to kill said hero and take their place.
It's an everyone-for-themselves free-for-all, yet there are opportunities for frantic 3v1 co-operative play — a necessity when all the non-hero ghost characters must take joint control of bosses the hero faces. It’s great fun in single-player thanks to some aggressive AI, but that consistent danger takes on a new dimension when you and three of your friends are jostling for XP and that all-important killing blow.
Competitive couchplay doesn’t get much better than this on Switch.
A roguelike at heart with a rhythm-game soul, Crypt Of The NecroDancer is a sublime experience that’s a must-play for fans of the genre(s).
Its upbeat, uptempo take on dungeon crawling is infectious, and there’s enough content here to last even the savviest of spelunkers for many, many dance-fuelled dives into the depths. If you’ve never tangoed with the NecroDancer, this fully-featured Switch edition is the perfect way to jump in.
For anybody who never played this but loved the Zelda spin-off Cadence of Hyrule and was left wanting more, what are you waiting for?

articles.title_orig: French authorities deploy 70,000 officers for Saturday protests; Louvre and other museums closed
articles.title_zh: French authorities deploy 70,000 officers for Saturday protests; Louvre and other museums closed
articles.content_orig:
Security forces to include elite units usually used for counter-terrorism after worst street violence in years
Europe live – latest updates
France will deploy about 70,000 police around the country on Saturday as the government seeks to prevent more civil unrest after some of the worst street violence in years erupted on the fringes of cost-of-living protests last weekend.
The interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said on ⁠Friday ⁠the security forces would include elite units usually used for counter-terrorism operations and hostage rescues, adding that there had been social media calls for violence from “ultra-left” groups.
“We are not talking about ⁠a peaceful, friendly demonstration,” Nuñez ​told reporters after a meeting of senior ministers and officials chaired by the president, Emmanuel Macron . “We ​are ​ready tomorrow ​to be ‌extremely firm ​and ​not tolerate anything.”
Macron and his government are struggling to get on top of a crisis that has caught it off guard six months before presidential elections to choose his successor. The government has admitted it “lost control” over widespread rioting on Saturday.
Largely peaceful demonstrations were hijacked by groups of determined rioters, degenerating into rampant violence and extensive looting in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities. In Limoges, the town hall was set on fire and partly destroyed.
“We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all who commit violence,” Nuñez said, adding that besides 10,000 more police, the operation would include water cannon, armoured vehicles, mounted police, helicopters and drones.
Demonstrations are expected in several other countries this weekend, triggered by a broader, continent-wide wave of discontent over declining public services, housing affordability, public sector budget cuts and the spiralling cost of living.
Protests over related grievances have been called for Saturday in Milan, Rome and Turin in Italy; in Vienna, Austria; and in Madrid, Barcelona and other cities in Spain, as well as in Lisbon and Porto in Portugal, Dublin in Ireland and Tirana in Albania.
Protests are expected across France on Saturday, although several cities have banned demonstrations or forced them to change their planned routes to protect shops and public buildings, and forecast heavy rain and high winds could dampen turnout.
The centres of Lyon and some other large cities will be off-limits to protesters, while authorities in Paris authorised a union march along a limited route in the east of the capital between the Places de la Bastille and Nation that will avoid the city centre.
But requests for rallies in Paris organised by France’s main student union, UNEF, and the gilets jaunes movement, whose nationwide protests rocked France in 2018 and which plans 600 small-scale events around France on Saturday, were refused.
UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and dilapidated facilities, would go ahead regardless. Several of the best-known cultural institutions in Paris, including the Louvre, said they would close on Saturday.
Authorities in Marseille had also banned all protests, but announced on Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis”. It will be the only authorised protest in the southern Bouches-du-Rhône department.
after newsletter promotion
Unionists and opposition leaders have criticised the government for refusing to allow more rallies on Saturday, a decision being challenged in court in several cities. Marylise Léon of the CFDT union federation accused Macron of an abuse of authority.
“It’s ​counterproductive because there is a lot ​of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to,” Léon, the CFDT’s general secretary, told TF1 TV. “It’s not for the president to decide who can legitimately protest.”
La France Insoumise, the radical left party of Jean-Luc Mélenchon, said the government had “crossed the lines that separate a democracy from an authoritarian and police state”, adding that the bans would only “generate more chaos”.
Adding to the tensions, the far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner for next spring’s presidential elections, is due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orléans, drawing thousands of supporters – and leftwing, anti-racist opponents.
Nuñez was due to visit the city on Friday to “inspect the security arrangements” at the request of the prime minister’s office. The justice minister, Gérald Darmanin, said 217 people – half of them first-time offenders – had been jailed since Saturday.
On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, saying gangs of rioters had been mainly responsible for the looting but the worst violence was caused by “ultra-left” groups seeking to “bring down the republic”.
Further stoking disquiet, one person was killed and four others injured – including a 12-year-old girl – in ⁠a shooting in the town of Trappes, west of Paris, on Friday in an attack that police said could have been racially motivated.

New for Necromunda in 2027
There’s an exciting year ahead for fans of Necromunda, with a lineup more stuffed than the questionably-sourced contents of a back-alley Scabber’s overcoat. There will be new miniatures, new terrain, new vehicles and new expansions. However, there won’t be a Roleplay expansion.
After careful consideration we’ve decided to focus our efforts on providing even more great minis for the core game.
Don’t worry – all the minis we showcased in the Big Autumn Preview are still on their way, and will be available for use in standard games of Necromunda.
Looking ahead to 2027, the new releases will cover multiple key gangs and locations, so here's a roadmap, because everybody loves roadmaps.*
Starting in the spring, we go back to the ash wastes with new rules expansions and the biggest plastic vehicle kit yet released for Necromunda.
Then, those brave enough can once more enter the cursed depths of the Underhells in search of ancient archeotech, where among other things they will bump into new Fighters for the Malstrain Genestealer cults.
And then we return to the still-smoking urban sprawl of Cinderak City, one of the conflict flashpoints of the recent Aranthian Succession . This is accompanied by support for some of the original underhive crews of Necromunda, including hulking new brutes.
And we’re still not done for 2027. Rounding out the year, there will be new mercenaries and gunslingers, set on hunting down their unfortunate bounties in whatever dank or irradiated corner of Necromunda they sought to hide.
Alongside all of the above, you’ll also get support for other gangs, scenery, and regular rules expansions.
And still set to arrive this year is a major expansion for the House of Iron in the shape of three flexible new multipart plastic kits, offering an enormous range of new cosmetic and wargear options for your Orlock gang.
We’ll cover them all in more detail soon, so check back regularly, and sign up to the Warhammer newsletter to stay up to date with the latest Necromunda news.

articles.title_orig: Weil Gotshal Loses More Top Lawyers as Merger Talks Collapse
articles.title_zh: Weil Gotshal Loses More Top Lawyers as Merger Talks Collapse
articles.content_orig:
Weil Gotshal & Manges and Willkie Farr & Gallagher have ended discussions over a possible merger, intensifying pressure on Weilâs leaders as many of its top partners take jobs elsewhere.
The talks were ended last night after the two sides had signed a non-disclosure agreement to discuss a tieup, two people familiar with the matter said. Willkie was the law firm Bloomberg Law reported Weil was in discussions with earlier this week.
On Thursday, at least some top partners at Weil had been holding discussions with their colleagues to build excitement for the possible tie-up, according to a person familiar with those discussions. By the end of the day, the merger talks were off.
The development came as more Weil partners headed for the exits.
The co-managing partner of Weilâs corporate department, Lyuba Goltser, plans to join Sidley Austin, according to a person familiar with the move. Davis Polk & Wardwell plans to bring on appellate litigator Drew Tulumello, another person said. And the Wall Street Journal reported Paul Weiss is hiring securities litigation partner Caroline Zalka. Tulumello and Zalka are members of Weilâs management committee.
It is unclear if Weil has lined up merger discussions with other firms, or whether its leaders will seek to do so. But continued departures of top partners risks setting off a so-called talent run, where partners begin to leave not because they can do better financially at another firm, but because they fear being left behind at a depleted firm.
âLateral movement for âI can do betterâ is very common,â said David McGowan, a law professor at the University of San Diego. âAnd the run on the bank metaphor happens when âI can do betterâ reaches a scale at which it turns into âI donât want to be left holding the bag.ââ
Some previous law firm mergers have come together after discussions broke down with early suitors.
Shearman & Sterling broke off talks with Hogan Lovells in 2023 before tying up with Allen & Overy. Kaye Scholer and Arnold & Porter in 2016 reportedly ended discussions, only for the talks to revive and the firms to merge.
Spokespeople for Weil and Willkie did not respond to requests for comment.
Large law firms in the US and UK have been actively exploring mergers in a race to scale and hot market for high-end corporate partners. A Weil combination with Willkie would have created a massive firm with more than $4 billion in annual revenue, placing it among the five largest based in the US.
Weil has been rocked by a string of partner departures in recent weeks, with more expected to be formally announced. The departures include Michael Aiello, the powerful corporate department leader who in September announced he would leave for Cravath, Swaine & Moore.

Helium producers in the United States will gain access to more federal financing and the government will keep a closer watch on the gas after the Energy Department designated it a critical material on Friday.
The Energy Department said the designation was made because helium is indispensable for making semiconductors that are essential to energy generation, and because the global supply is at risk of disruption.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Trump administration is freeing America from reliance on foreign sources of critical materials, strengthening domestic manufacturing, supporting American jobs and securing the materials essential to U.S. economic and national security.
“President Trump is bringing back America’s manufacturing industry, and that means making sure we have the materials needed to build things in America again,” Wright said in a statement.
Helium is the 20th critical material identified by the department. Metallurgical coal used for steelmaking was the last substance to be added to the list, in 2025. Fluorine is the only other gas on it.
To qualify, a non-fuel mineral element or substance must serve an essential function in one or more energy technologies, and there must be a high risk of disruption to the supply chain.
The designation matters for reasons that go well beyond party balloons, even though helium is what makes them rise. The department points to the gas's role in wind, solar and nuclear energy production, space exploration, medical imaging and research.
Assistant Secretary of Energy Audrey Robertson said helium's unique properties make it irreplaceable, citing the facts that it is non-combustible and has the lowest boiling point of any gas. Robertson, who oversees the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, added that the nation needs an ample supply for semiconductors, quantum and super computing, and superconducting magnets.
“We need to make sure that we can build those here. And helium is one of those components that could be a single point of failure, where we cannot let that happen. That’s why we’re designating it within our statutory authority, but I think why it’s important is not necessarily for our birthday parties,” Robertson said in an interview. “It’s really towards the future of American competitiveness and energy security, which we believe is national security.”
The supply risks behind the designation are concentrated abroad. Qatar's helium exports have been severely curtailed by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a result of its war with Israel and the U.S.
Iranian strikes on Qatar's infrastructure have also affected supply. Russia, one of the other top helium producers alongside the United States, imposed temporary export controls on helium in April to protect its domestic supply.
The United States is the world's largest producer of both natural gas and helium, and helium is primarily produced as a byproduct of natural gas processing. Even so, U.S. output is constrained.
The country produced 81 million cubic meters of helium in 2025, or 43% of the global supply, and exported 38 million cubic meters of that. Annual production has run at roughly 80 million cubic meters since 2021.
Large reserves sit in Wyoming, Kansas, Texas, Oklahoma, Colorado and Utah. But according to the department, helium extraction plants are at their limits, and it takes years to permit and build new ones, which continues to constrain U.S. production.
Federal data shows the plants extracting the most helium, as of 2023, were located in Kansas, Texas, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona and Oklahoma. The constraints have a historical dimension.
The United States once kept a strategic national stockpile of helium in Texas, much like the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Congress mandated in 2013 that it be privatized, and the Bureau of Land Management completed the sale of the federal helium system to the industrial gas company Messer in 2024.
Some in the helium industry had urged the government to make the designation formal. The North American gas exploration company Avanti Helium Corp. says it is urgent, and that an increase in North American supply is needed to avoid becoming dependent on foreign sources.
The U.S. Geological Survey included helium on a 2018 list of critical minerals, but later lists omitted it because the domestic supply of helium was considered secure. The United States designates both critical minerals and critical materials, and there is some crossover between the two lists.
Greeshma Gadikota, director of the Lenfast Center for Sustainable Energy at Columbia University, said that despite environmental concerns with recovering helium from natural gas, there are also opportunities.
“If we burn the natural gas, there are a lot of CO2 emissions associated with that,” Gadikota said. "But if you just extract the helium and use it, the uses of it don't contribute necessarily to greenhouse gas emissions.
“So from a climate standpoint, if we are going to continue down the line of extracting natural gas and recovering helium," she added, “I would prefer to see natural gas being used in a form where we directly produce hydrogen and we produce solid carbon.” Hydrogen is a clean burning fuel, and solid carbon can provide permanent carbon sequestration.
“We can effectively consolidate everything from raw materials to finished product in terms of manufacturing in the United States and rely less on overseas,” Gadikota said. "It brings more refining, recovery, use capabilities to the U.S. and actually justifies any investments of U.S. taxpayer dollars in initiatives related to helium production and refining."

Oops, something went wrong
Some companies don't keep their ambitions secret. They swagger onto the stock market and draw plenty of attention with a splashy IPO and big promises (lookin' at you, Tesla ).
But some incredibly successful stocks are sleeper hits: They quietly sit on the market doing nothing until one day, bam! Their shares take off like a rocket, and everybody wonders how they didn't see it coming.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
That's what happened to memory chipmaker Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) in late 2025: Its shares had languished for years until a global memory shortage and AI data center boom took the stock stratospheric. Between June 25, 2025, and June 25, 2026, the chipmaker's shares grew more than 850%.
If you were lucky enough to invest $10,000 in Micron on that day in 2025, you'd have had $95,370 a year later. Even today, after shares have dropped 25% from those highs, you'd still have $70,970. Not enough, perhaps, to fund a full retirement, but a nice chunk of change.
So, what about right now? Could buying $10,000 in Micron today set you up for life?
It's ironic that even though Micron's share price has grown astronomically since June 2025, its price-to-earnings ratio -- how its share price compares to its profits -- has actually gone down. In June 2025, shares were trading at about 22 times earnings. In June 2026, at its peak, it traded at about 27 times earnings. Today, it's trading at about 12 times earnings.
Why would a wildly successful company that's grown its revenue by 256% and its per-share earnings by 879% in 16 months have a cheaper valuation than it did before?
The simple answer is that the market doesn't expect the good times to last, for two reasons.
The first reason is that this has happened before to memory chip stocks, and it didn't end well. Prices for dynamic RAM (DRAM) memory spiked in 2020-2021 during the pandemic tech-buying surge. After expanding capacity to meet that demand, memory producers wound up with a supply glut, and prices crashed in 2023.
This time around, Micron has tried to protect itself against such a price crash by signing multiyear supply deals with its customers to lock in price floors, allowing it to safely expand its capacity. That's a smart move, but the market is also concerned about competition.
Until now, three companies have had the global market for DRAM and high bandwidth memory (HBM) to themselves: Micron and South Korean companies Samsung Electronics (OTC: SSNLF) and SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY). But all three are planning to expand capacity, while concerns about rapid expansion by Chinese manufacturers abound.
While it's possible that Micron's long-term contracts will allow it to continue to grow revenue and profits, a nervous market is unlikely to give it full credit for its success. It certainly seems doubtful that it will reach a $10 trillion valuation anytime soon (which would turn a $10,000 investment into $100,000).
Even if a $10,000 investment in Micron probably won't set you up for life, the ongoing growth of AI infrastructure deployment should make Micron a solid investment for years to come.

articles.content_orig:
A drone has hit a commercial ship off the coast of Romania, killing at least one crew member with three more still missing, Romanian President Nicușor Dan said Friday.
“This morning we experienced a security incident: A vessel was struck by a drone approximately 13 nautical miles from the coast, just beyond Romania’s territorial waters,” Dan said, praising the coast guard for saving nine sailors as part of the rescue operation. “Unfortunately, one sailor has died and three others are still being searched for,” he added.
The Khoryv ship, flying under the flag of Comoros, suffered significant damage, capsized and partially sank, according to Romania’s Interior Ministry.
The incident is the latest in a string of drone attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Dan told POLITICO last week that Russia’s intention was clearly to weaken Romania’s support for Ukraine in the war but vowed not to back down.
NATO allies met Tuesday to discuss the threat to Black Sea shipping and Dan said Romania would receive “additional capabilities” to help defend the area.
“Evidently, this is an incident within the broader process of escalation that Russia is pursuing in the context of its war in Ukraine,” the Romanian president said.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she was “deeply alarmed” by “yet another Russian escalation in the Black Sea.” The ship was carrying Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew, she said.
“These reckless attacks target innocent lives and openly defy international law. My thoughts are with the family and loved ones of the sailor that was killed. And with the families of the three crew members still missing.”
Over the last month, drones have hit several cargo ships and chemical tankers close to Romania and Bulgaria — both NATO members — killing more than 20 people in total.
Reuters reported that the ships hit by drones in recent weeks had been near or heading towards the Sulina Canal, linking the Danube River and the Black Sea. This has become a key export route for Ukrainian grain and food oil after Russia attacked Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports.

While the future of former Xbox first-party devs like Double Fine and Undead Labs has already been determined, it’s been a while since we heard word from Arkane Lyon , the studio behind the acclaimed Dishonored games.
Now an article by Le Monde (paywalled) gives an insight into the struggles of the French studio, as it races to find a buyer before a 13th November deadline.
As you may recall, Microsoft was unable to close the studio immediately due to a consultation period demanded by French law. The Redmond firm is obligated to try to sell the studio, but a mandated three month deadline is now coming to a close.
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
The team has until 13th November to find new funding, otherwise the studio will be shuttered and around 217 jobs will be lost. According to the report, negotiations are ongoing.
Union representatives claim the team’s current project, Marvel’s Blade – which was announced in 2023 – is “nearing the end of production”. Spokespeople for the studio believe it will be a success if it sees the light of day.
But those same people blame Microsoft for its “disrespectful” treatment of the team.
“We are collateral victims of Xbox’s change in strategy,” one of the people said.
As alluded to above, Microsoft has already shuttered UK studio Ninja Theory , and offloaded various other teams like Compulsion Games et al.
It’s also in the process of reorganising its entire first-party operations, seemingly sunsetting Xbox Game Studios as it places its remaining teams under the umbrella of Bethesda and Activision. Its objective is to focus on big franchises like Fallout and Call of Duty .
The scary part is that the platform holder is not done yet: it’s cut over 1,800 jobs so far, but more redundancies are coming , as it aims to eliminate 3,200 roles overall.

articles.title_orig: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.title_zh: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.content_orig:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda , Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
The new information contradicts accounts from Uganda, which previously said the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo, and will raise concerns about the ability of authorities to contain the outbreak, which is already the most geographically widespread in history.
The Ugandan government reported Ebola cases in May and June before WHO declared it Ebola-free in August. A Ugandan government spokesperson told Reuters on Thursday that Uganda had no ​Ebola cases and that, if ​it did, it would make that information ​public.
The World Health Organization said investigations were continuing to establish the likely source of infection for the Ebola patient in Nigeria.
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention is investigating whether the patient may have come into contact with an Ebola patient in Kenya, as both travelled from Uganda’s Entebbe airport on 3 October, said Dr Wessam Mankoula, head of emergency preparedness and response at the organisation.
Catherine Smallwood, a WHO Ebola incident manager in DR Congo, told a UN briefing in Geneva via video ‌link on Friday that WHO staff in DR Congo had no information showing the patient in Nigeria had travelled to the country.
Smallwood said a link to the case in Kenya was possible, ​but added that officials would need to compare the timing with when the Nigeria patient’s symptoms began to tell whether the infection more likely happened at the Ugandan airport or elsewhere.
Marion Koopmans, a Dutch virologist and member of the WHO’s Ebola emergency committee, cast doubt on the theory. “I think that is very speculative unless there is evidence of sharing the same ​space in a manner that could explain that,” she said. “Random presence at the same location, a large airport, is not a supported epidemiological link by any standard of what we currently know.”
The Nigerian health minister, Muhammad Ali Pate, said Nigeria’s case remains contained and that contact-tracing was continuing. “We are trying to contain it so it doesn’t go out to the communities. Hopefully, it won’t get to that and we are working hard to ensure that,” Pate said.
Melaku Yirga, vice-president for Africa at Prosper Global (formerly Mercy Corps), said the confirmation of Ebola in Kenya and Nigeria reinforces the need for countries to work closely together to prevent further transmission.
“What matters most now is speed, sharing information across borders without delay and ensuring frontline health workers and local organiaations have the resources to respond quickly,” he said.
Ebola is a highly contagious and often fatal viral disease that affects humans and non-human primates. It spreads through body fluids or contaminated materials and causes organ damage, blood vessel impairment and sometimes severe internal and external bleeding.
The current outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine. It was first announced on 15 May and has infected more than 9,500 people and killed nearly half of them.
The outbreak is the largest and deadliest in DR Congo’s history and second only ​globally to ​the 2014-16 outbreak in west Africa, which infected ​more than ‌28,600 people ​and ​killed more than 11,000.

articles.title_zh: Volvo Shares Plunge as China Ambitions Fade for Western Carmakers
articles.content_orig:
Volvo Cars said Friday it plans to cut 2,500 jobs after a sharp decline in its Chinese market weighed on third-quarter earnings.
The Swedish automaker reported an operating loss of 5.6 billion Swedish kronor ($563.7 million) in the third quarter, down from an operating profit of 6.4 billion Swedish kronor in the previous period.
The company, which is owned by China's Geely Holding, cited a deteriorating environment led by "tougher" market conditions in China and the U.S., which "negatively affected free cash flow."
Volvo Cars shares were 24.2% lower at the end of the trading session.
"It's really a lot about the Chinese market, of course, where the change has come faster than we thought, and really now we can see that selling global cars developed in Europe and China will not work, and then this is affecting all the Western players in China," Volvo Cars CEO Håkan Samuelsson told CNBC on "Squawk Box Europe," on Friday.
Chinese consumers are now looking for "domestic alternatives," which have become stronger and more competitive, the CEO said. "We need a new strategy in China... it has to be a more regional structure, a more empowered region, and we need regionally adapted cars."
He added that costs must be competitive and that Volvo Cars needs to share some platforms with its Chinese parent company Geely, and develop key software in China that includes infotainment and driver-assistance systems. "If you don't have that, I think you cannot sell cars in China."
Volvo Cars' revenues in China fell almost 50% year-on-year as premium brands faced "hypercompetition" from new Chinese rivals, which also put severe pressure on pricing, the company said.
Meanwhile, in the U.S., the automaker cited negative effects from tariffs and fewer customer incentives to buy electric cars, putting pressure on profit margins.
Volvo Cars said it is looking to cut 5 billion Swedish kronor in costs and will eliminate 2,500 jobs globally, with 2,000 of those jobs based in Sweden.
"It is really a consequence of this development, our long-range strategy," Samuelsson told CNBC. "We will have more empowered, stronger regions, and then of course you cannot keep the same resources on the corporate central level. So we need a leaner central administration."

China’s domestic online beauty sales are falling as C-beauty companies are ramping up export efforts and moving into international retail channels. The gap suggests a deliberate pivot from C-beauty toward overseas growth, targeting the categories and regions that K-beauty has spent the past decade winning over.
According to Jefferies’ China online beauty tracker , the country recorded a 6% year-on-year cosmetics sales decline in September 2026. Skin care fell 6.1%, while color cosmetics went down 5.2%.
However, at the same time, data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) shows China climbing from seventh place to fifth in global cosmetics exports. The trade body says China’s color cosmetics exports amount to nearly three times that of Korea’s.
C-beauty company Proya, meanwhile, has opened a European Innovation Center Laboratory in France and has announced it will begin selling across 400 Ulta Beauty stores in the US next month.
“This Europe Innovation Center Laboratory connects the European and Chinese ecosystems to draw on combined strengths and create new innovation capabilities,” says Hou Juncheng, founder and chairman of Proya Cosmetics.
The center is not the first bridge between Chinese and European beauty. French ingredient suppliers have been actively pursuing partnerships with Chinese cosmetics brands, and many Chinese perfumers train in France. The country’s Cosmetic Valley, meanwhile, has set up a Shanghai-based fragrance and cosmetics embassy to encourage collaboration between the two markets . Chinese beauty brands are expanding overseas, targeting markets where K-beauty has established a strong presence.
With color cosmetics exports already outpacing Korea’s and a growing foothold in US and European retail, C-beauty appears to be borrowing the playbook that got K-beauty onto global shelves.
The September figures from Jefferies’ tracker show many multinational beauty giants experiencing declining figures in China. L’Oréal fell 5%, Estée Lauder 8%, Procter & Gamble 20%, Shiseido 24%, and LVMH 26%.
Beiersdorf and Galderma were the only multinationals to grow, supported by their Nivea and Cetaphil brands. At the brand level, dermatological skin care like CeraVe and Cetaphil grew (35% and 58%, respectively), while Bobbi Brown fell 31%. Among domestic players, Mao Geping grew 26%, and Proya grew 1%.
As demand becomes increasingly selective, and derma-brands gain ground, Jefferies’ findings show skin care and color cosmetics accounting for over 80% of China’s beauty market. Both categories initially gave rise to K-beauty.
According to KITA, China’s cosmetic exports reached ₩8.14 trillion (US$6.1 billion) from January to July 2026, up 24% from ₩6.55 trillion (US$4.9 billion) a year earlier. The figures lifted China to fifth in global export rankings, behind France in the lead and South Korea in second place.
In color cosmetics, China has already overtaken Korea. Exports of lip and eye makeup, powders, and nail products totaled ₩1.88 trillion (US$1.41 billion) from January to July, about 2.9 times Korea’s ₩644.7 billion (US$484 million).
From January to July 2026, China’s lip makeup exports were 1.7 times Korea’s, and its eye makeup exports were 3.5 times. China’s exports grew 17% to 33% across all four color cosmetics categories (lip, eye, powders, and nail products), while Korea’s lip makeup and nail product exports fell 15% and 15.6%, respectively. Proya is expanding its international presence with a new research laboratory in France.
According to The Asia Business Daily, Kecia Steelman, CEO of Ulta Beauty, raised C-beauty during the company’s 2026 Q2 fiscal earnings call. She is quoted as saying, “[We are launching] Proya, the number one skin care brand in China. So it’s not just about K-Beauty anymore.”
Proya’s US launch will be the first time a Chinese premium skin care brand joins Ulta’s online and physical networks at the same time. The rollout is planned for November this year, and with it, Proya says it is “moving beyond mere product export to brand globalization.”
To expand, the company says, “brands must not only enter overseas markets but also earn a permanent place in consumers’ daily skin care regimens and secure a voice within elite global beauty narratives.”
Securing that voice, Proya has inaugurated its Europe Innovation Center Laboratory in France, with a 450 square meter site containing 76 pieces of equipment and seven dedicated researchers. The lab will focus on research and innovation in skin longevity, biology, biotechnology, and sustainable ingredients.
The lab will collaborate with the Hangzhou Longwu center in China, which handles formulation, ingredients, safety, and efficacy, and the Shanghai center, which works on hair care and the scalp microbiome.
Proya’s international push comes after its namesake brand, which accounts for around 70% of group revenue, posted a 7% sales decline in H1 2026. The drop was the company’s first after years of uninterrupted growth since its 2017 Shanghai listing. Jefferies says the brand returned to 1% growth in September, but the overseas expansion appears partly aimed at offsetting soft momentum.
